publisher: American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS)
abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Enhancing the nutritional value of food crops is a means of improving human nutrition and health. We report here the positional cloning of
                    <jats:italic>Gpc-B1</jats:italic>
                    , a wheat quantitative trait locus associated with increased grain protein, zinc, and iron content. The ancestral wild wheat allele encodes a NAC transcription factor (
                    <jats:italic>NAM-B1</jats:italic>
                    ) that accelerates senescence and increases nutrient remobilization from leaves to developing grains, whereas modern wheat varieties carry a nonfunctional
                    <jats:italic>NAM-B1</jats:italic>
                    allele. Reduction in RNA levels of the multiple
                    <jats:italic>NAM</jats:italic>
                    homologs by RNA interference delayed senescence by more than 3 weeks and reduced wheat grain protein, zinc, and iron content by more than 30%.
                  </jats:p>
title: A NAC Gene Regulating Senescence Improves Grain Protein, Zinc, and Iron Content in Wheat

The paralogous TtNAM-A2 copy was not detected in the LDN tetraploid BAC library or by PCR with 2A genome specific primers derived from T. urartu where the TuNAM-A2 gene is present.

The Bobwhite TaNAM-B1 gene is deleted as determined by PCR with four sets of independent NAM-B1 specific primers (table S5). Therefore no expression data are included for TaNAM-B1 in the transgenic plants.
Field experiments including Gpc-B1 isogenic lines showed a more variable effect of the DIC chromosome region (including TtNAM-B1 ) on grain size ( 14 ).
